audit.why: 52.23% over 3123 games, the largest sample in my slice. You win the duel at every stage and lose the game to his teamfight utility — the page already draws that distinction cleanly.
Spikes are placed right: your 1-3, his level 6 Depth Charge gank window, and the two-item stage where his CC scales past your duelling. This page is better written than most in the slice.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings tell you to hold Aegis Assault to 'block his hook line' and 'face his Dredge Line'. Aegis Assault cannot stop a hook.
audit.why: Riot's text: Pantheon 'sets his shield, becoming invulnerable to damage from the front'. That is damage, and only from the front. Dredge Line 'colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together' — the pull is displacement and hard CC, so it lands through the shield and cancels the channel outright, leaving you pulled in with your longest cooldown spent for nothing. The page recommends this three times as the answer to his only engage. It is the worst possible response to it. Dredge Line is also 1150 range against Shield Vault's 600, so he can open from nearly twice your reach.
audit.corrected: Aegis Assault's role narrowed to Riptide damage, and the hook answer changed to sidestepping it, with the pull's channel cancel stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Staggering Blow and Titan's Wrath are never mentioned, and between them they explain most of what goes wrong in a trade.
audit.why: Staggering Blow is 'Nautilus' first Attack against a target deals increased physical damage and roots them briefly'. His very first auto-attack roots you — which means it cancels Aegis Assault without him spending a single ability, and it means he never needs the hook to lock you for the follow-up. That is the highest-value missing fact on this page. Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield with damage over time attached, and it is the reason your burst stops landing at level 3 despite the page saying his tank base is thin.
audit.corrected: Staggering Blow's root and its effect on your channel written into mid and whys[2]; Titan's Wrath named in the level-3 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns, so 'once his R is on cooldown, go back to bullying him' has no duration attached.
audit.why: Depth Charge is 120/100/80s and Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10s — those two numbers are the entire respect-and-punish rhythm of the lane. Riptide is 7s down to 5s, so his chip is always available and is not worth waiting out.

edits.before: With Q poke, W stun and Aegis Assault (E) you out-trade him cleanly — your E blocks his Dredge Line (Q) and tanks his E spam while you stack Mortal Will.
edits.after: With all three basics you out-trade him — Aegis Assault eats Riptide, though Titan's Wrath is a 12s shield that soaks the first half of your burst.

edits.after: Sidestep Dredge Line at its 1150 range, and save Aegis Assault for his Riptide instead

edits.before: Land Dredge Line (Q) hook to pull you in and flip the short trade onto his terms
edits.after: Hook you from 1150, or just auto once — Staggering Blow roots on his first hit

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. Your point-and-click Shield Vault (W) stun out-damages his Dredge Line (Q) hook at level 1, and once you hit your W+Q level-2 spike you can all-in before his E is up to peel minions off you. Hold Aegis Assault (E) for his Q — block the hook line and his E AoE while you tap-Q reset autos. His only real answer is landing a raw hook, so sidestep it and the lane is one-sided.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. Point-and-click Shield Vault out-damages Dredge Line at level 1, and your level-2 spike all-ins before Riptide can peel minions off you. Do not hold Aegis Assault for the hook: it only stops damage from the front, and the pull is displacement that lands anyway and cancels the channel. Save it for Riptide. Sidestep the hook instead — it reaches 1150 to your 600, so respect that range and the lane is one-sided.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay favoured — empowered-Q poke chips his low tank base while E eats his E spam, and he can't trade back without burning his hook. Level 6 is the one window I respect: Depth Charge (R) is an undodgeable knockup that, chained off his passive root, gives his jungler a free kill, so back off the wave when his ult is up and he has help nearby. Once his R is on cooldown, go back to bullying him.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay favoured — empowered Comet Spear chips him while Aegis Assault eats Riptide. But he does not need Dredge Line to lock you: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against you, so one auto cancels your channel for free. Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 and Depth Charge 120s, and that pair is the whole rhythm — back off the wave while the ult is up and his jungler is near, then bully him for the next two minutes.

edits.before: Your first-item spike still beats a tank Nautilus one-on-one, so keep pressing — that's your last clean window to cash the lead into towers and roams. By 2+ items the math flips: his chain-CC (hook, root, Depth Charge) only gets more reliable in teamfights while your raw dueling damage plateaus. Don't try to solo-kill a fed tank late; convert your early tempo with Grand Starfall (R) roams and end before his utility takes over the game.
edits.after: Your first-item spike still beats a tank Nautilus one-on-one, so keep pressing — that is the last clean window to cash the lead into towers and roams. By 2+ items it flips: Dredge Line, Staggering Blow's root and Depth Charge chain into each other in every teamfight while your duelling damage plateaus. Don't solo-kill a fed tank late; convert the early tempo with Grand Starfall roams and end before his utility runs the game.

notes: THE FINDING: three strings told the player to hold Aegis Assault to block Dredge Line. It cannot. Riot's text has Pantheon 'invulnerable to damage from the front', and Dredge Line's pull is displacement and hard CC — it lands through the shield and cancels the channel, so following that advice means being pulled in with your 22-second cooldown already spent. The page recommended it as the answer to his only engage. Second and larger: Staggering Blow is never mentioned anywhere. His first attack against a target roots them, which means a single auto-attack cancels Aegis Assault without him spending an ability at all, and he does not need the hook to set up his combo. That is the most useful missing fact on this page. Also added Titan's Wrath, a flat 12s shield that explains why your burst stops landing at 3 even though the page calls his tank base thin, and the range gap that makes his engage possible — Dredge Line reaches 1150 against Shield Vault's 600. The packet's suspectName on 'His Depth Charge' in whys[4] is a FALSE POSITIVE; that is the correct name.
